answer: Resist Sybils with a concurrent liveness audit. At an unpredictable moment each epoch, drawn from a public beacon no one can whisper ahead, the network fires one timed challenge at a random subset of identities at once. Each must return a signed answer from fresh randomness in a tight window. An operator running many aliases on shared machines cannot serve a comet of simultaneous challenges in time, since one machine serializes, so colocated clones miss and forfeit stake. A genuine agent on its own island of resources answers once. Cost scales with distinct machines, not account count.
